'''Walter Kaminsky''' (7 May 1941 – 23 November 2024) was a German chemist who specialised in [[olefin]] [[polymerization]] and [[plastic recycling]]. He discovered the high activity of Group 4 [[metallocene]]/[[methylaluminoxane]] (MAO) mixtures (later named the [[Kaminsky catalyst]]) as [[catalyst]]s for olefin polymerization in 1980.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 May 2024 |title=Dr. Walter Kaminsky: Pioneer of Catalysts Revolutionizing Polymer Production and Recycling |url=https://www.ptonline.com/articles/dr-walter-kaminsky-pioneer-of-catalysts-revolutionizing-polymer-production-and-recycling |access-date=19 June 2024 |website=www.ptonline.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Kaminsky was born in [[Hamburg]], [[Nazi Germany|Germany]] on 7 May 1941. He studied chemistry at the [[University of Hamburg]]. He received his PhD under Hansjörg Sinn in 1978 and obtained his habilitation in 1982, both at the [[University of Hamburg]]. He was a faculty member at the [[University of Hamburg]] since 1977, and later became a full professor for Technical and [[polymer chemistry|Macromolecular Chemistry]]. He retired and became an emeritus professor in 2006.

He was awarded, among other prizes, the [[Körber European Science Prize]] in 1988, the [[The Franklin Institute Awards|1999 Benjamin Franklin Medal]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Walter Kaminsky|url=https://www.fi.edu/laureates/walter-kaminsky|website=The Franklin Institute|date=10 January 2014 |accessdate=6 September 2017}}</ref> and the [[Hermann Staudinger Prize]] 2002. In 2024, he was inducted into the Plastics Hall of Fame.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Walter Kaminsky |url=https://plasticshof.org/members/dr-walter-kaminsky/ |access-date=19 June 2024 |website=plasticshof.org}}</ref>

Kaminsky died on 23 November 2024, at the age of 83.<ref>[https://hamburgertrauer.de/traueranzeige/walter-kaminsky Walter Kaminsky] {{in lang|de}}</ref>
